headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network privileges create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and conflicting writes between Cline and Plandex.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Plandex shares state via filesystem and can read/write the project directory. That creates a default content bridge where one agent can ingest the other's outputs as trusted text. No stronger isolation is documented, so the interaction is plausible in normal use.
conditions: IF Cline writes instructions into workspace files that Plandex later reads
IF Plandex writes plan artifacts into the shared project directory that Cline parses as guidance
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable auto-ingest of generated files
Use a read-only handoff file for inter-agent exchange
Review shared files before either agent consumes them
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and both have broad network egress, so shared workspace data can flow into either model backend during normal operation. Cline also handles browser screenshots, increasing the chance that sensitive content in the workspace or browser context is exposed to Plandex through copied artifacts or shared files.
conditions: IF browser screenshots or secrets are stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent uploads file contents to its inference backend during routine use
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Use separate API keys and accounts
Redact screenshots before saving them
Restrict network egress during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and modify_git_state in overlapping workspace/project directories. Cline shares state via filesystem and Plandex stages changes in a plan-local sandbox before apply, but neither profile shows locking across the pair. Concurrent edits can corrupt git state or overwrite each other's files by default.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same file or branch in the same workspace
IF one agent applies staged changes while the other is modifying git state
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file-level ownership conventions
Run git status before every apply
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but Cline can emit browser-derived or file-derived outputs that Plandex may treat as planning input. Because both are autonomous coding tools, an error in Cline's output can cascade into Plandex's staged changes unless manually verified.
conditions: IF Plandex consumes Cline-generated files without human review
IF Cline's browser or file outputs are used as authoritative facts for Plandex plans
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Cross-check generated facts against source files
Limit Cline output to summaries
Keep Plandex in review-only mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The main compliance concern is operational rather than contractual: shared source code and screenshots may be retained in different places, but the profiles do not document a specific policy conflict. Cline is not cited separately because no unique compliance gap is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared workspace files
IF one agent's backend retains data longer than the other in an undocumented way
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Check retention settings for both backends
Use separate projects for sensitive work
Delete temporary artifacts after use
requires-engineering: document and enforce retention policy
